Wilder Lavington1,2 , Justice Sefas1,2 , Matthew Niedoba1,2 , Yunpeng Liu1,2 , Berend Zwartsenberg1 , Setareh Dabiri1 , Frank Wood1,2,3 , Adam Ścibior1 1 Inverted AI, 2 University of British Columbia, 3 Mila; ∗ vasileios.lioutas@inverted.ai

extractions.description: This paper introduces CriticSMC, a novel algorithm that combines sequential Monte Carlo with learned Soft-Q function heuristic factors to enhance planning efficiency in environments with sparse hard constraints, such as collision avoidance in autonomous driving. CriticSMC employs these heuristic factors to guide the sampling process in order to improve inference and planning, making it particularly useful for AI applications in self-driving vehicles.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on improving the efficiency of autonomous driving through a new planning algorithm, CriticSMC. Autonomous driving is directly related to Climate Change Mitigation under the Transportation sub-category since improving the efficiency and safety of autonomous vehicles could contribute to reducing emissions and reliance on traditional fuel sources.
primary_category.quote: Our experiments on collision avoidance in a high-dimensional simulated driving task show that CriticSMC significantly reduces collision rates at a low computational cost while maintaining realism and diversity of driving behaviors across vehicles and environment scenarios.

secondary_categories.justification: The focus of the paper is primarily on improving autonomous driving algorithms, which does not directly align with any other specific eco-responsible categories beyond the transportation implication.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper aims to enhance the planning capabilities in autonomous driving scenarios, which falls under the Transportation sub-category of Climate Change Mitigation. The enhanced algorithms aim to reduce collisions and improve autonomous driving efficiency.
primary_sub_category.quote: We show experimentally that CriticSMC is able to refine the policy of a foundation (Bommasani et al., 2021) autonomous-driving behavior model to take actions that produce significantly fewer collisions while retaining key behavioral distribution characteristics of the foundation model.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: While the paper could have broader implications, its current focus does not fit into any other specific eco-responsible sub-category besides Transportation.

applications.justification: The paper specifically discusses the application of CriticSMC in reducing collision rates and improving planning efficiency in autonomous driving, making it a clear application of the research.
applications.quote: Our experiments on collision avoidance in a high-dimensional simulated driving task show that CriticSMC significantly reduces collision rates at a low computational cost.

applications.justification: CriticSMC improves planning in environments with sparse constraints, which is crucial for the development and operation of autonomous vehicles.
applications.quote: CriticSMC is compatible with informative priors...and can be used as a model-free control algorithm...important not only for the eventual goal of learning complete autonomous driving policies.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories and sub-categories adequately capture the focus of the paper, which is on transportation within the context of climate change mitigation.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The focus on autonomous driving and collision avoidance is well covered under the existing Transportation sub-category, and no new sub-category is needed.
